dhpak1.14:1.1: 1.13 The Story about Queen Sumanā Sumanādeviyā Vatthu
dhpak1.14:2.1: “Here she’s happy, after death she’s happy,” {1.151} this Dhamma teaching was given
dhpak1.14:2.2: by the Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to Queen Sumanā.
dhpak1.14:3.1: For every day 2,000 bhikkhus take their meal in the house of Anāthapiṇḍika at Sāvatthī, and a like number in the house of the eminent
dhpak1.14:3.2: female lay disciple Visākhā. Whoever desires to give alms at Sāvatthī, first seeks the good offices of these two lay disciples.
dhpak1.14:3.3: Do you ask the reason for this? Suppose you are asked the question: “Has Anāthapiṇḍika or Visākhā given alms equal in amount to those which you have given?”
dhpak1.14:3.4: and you answer: “They have not,” you may dispense 100,000 coins in alms, and in spite of this the bhikkhus will murmur dissatisfaction,
dhpak1.14:3.5: saying: “What kind of alms are these?” The explanation is that both of these lay disciples understand thoroughly the tastes of
dhpak1.14:3.6: the Saṅgha of bhikkhus and [28.243] know exactly what is the proper thing to do; therefore all who desire to give alms take them
dhpak1.14:3.7: with them when they go. And thus it happens that they are unable to minister to the bhikkhus in person in their own houses.
dhpak1.14:4.1: Under these circumstances Visākhā, considering within herself: “Who shall stand in my place and minister to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?”
dhpak1.14:4.2: seeing the daughter of her son, appointed her to represent her; and thenceforth Visākhā’s granddaughter ministered to the
dhpak1.14:4.3: Saṅgha of bhikkhus in Visākhā’s residence. Anāthapiṇḍika appointed his oldest daughter Mahā Subhaddā;
dhpak1.14:4.4: the latter showed the bhikkhus the customary attentions, hearkened to the Dhamma, and as a result obtained Stream-entry;
dhpak1.14:4.5: afterwards she married and went to live with her husband’s family. Then he appointed Culla Subhaddā, who followed her older sister’s example,
dhpak1.14:4.6: obtaining Stream-entry, and afterwards marrying and going to live with the family of her husband.
dhpak1.14:4.7: Finally he appointed his youngest daughter Sumanā. Sumanā obtained the fruition of Once-returning, but remained unmarried.
dhpak1.14:4.8: {1.152} Overwhelmed with disappointment at her failure to obtain a husband, she refused to eat, and desiring to see her father, sent for him.
dhpak1.14:5.1: Three Daughters Anāthapiṇḍika was in the refectory when he received his daughter’s message, but immediately went to her and said:
dhpak1.14:5.2: “What is it, dear daughter Sumanā?” Sumanā said to him: “What say you, dear youngest brother?”
dhpak1.14:5.3: – “You talk incoherently, dear daughter.” – “I am not talking incoherently, youngest brother.”
dhpak1.14:5.4: – “Are you afraid, dear daughter?” – “I am not afraid, youngest brother.” She said no more, but died immediately.
dhpak1.14:6.1: Although the rich man had obtained Stream-entry, he was unable to bear the grief that arose within him. Accordingly,
dhpak1.14:6.2: when he had performed the funeral rites over his daughter’s body, he went weeping to the Teacher. The Teacher said: “Householder,
dhpak1.14:6.3: how is it that you come to me sad and sorrowful, with tears in your eyes, weeping?” – “Venerable Sir, my daughter Sumanā is dead.”
dhpak1.14:6.4: – “Well, why do you weep? Is not death certain for all?” – “I know that, venerable Sir. But my daughter was so modest and so conscientious.
dhpak1.14:6.5: What grieves me so much is the thought that when she died, she was unable to recover her right mind, but died speaking incoherently.”
dhpak1.14:7.1: What grieves me “But what did your youngest daughter say, rich man?” – “Venerable Sir, I addressed her as ‘dear Sumanā,’
dhpak1.14:7.2: and she replied: ‘What say you, dear youngest brother?’ Then I said to her: ‘You talk [28.244] incoherently,
dhpak1.14:7.3: dear daughter.’ – ‘I am not talking incoherently, youngest brother.’ – ‘Are you afraid, dear daughter?’
dhpak1.14:7.4: – ‘I am not afraid, youngest brother.’ She said no more, but died immediately.”
dhpak1.14:8.1: Said the Fortunate One to Anāthapiṇḍika: “Rich man, your daughter did not talk incoherently.” – “But why did she speak thus?”
dhpak1.14:8.2: – “Solely because you were her younger brother. {1.153} Householder, your daughter was old in the paths and the fruitions,
dhpak1.14:8.3: for while you have attained but Stream-entry, your daughter had attained the fruit of Once-returning. Thus it was, because she was old
dhpak1.14:8.4: in the paths and the fruitions, that she spoke thus.” – “Was that the reason, venerable Sir?” – “That was the reason, householder.”
dhpak1.14:9.1: “Where has she now been reborn, venerable Sir?” – “In the world of the Tusita gods, householder.” – “Venerable Sir,
dhpak1.14:9.2: while my daughter remained here among her kinsfolk, she went about rejoicing, and when she went hence, she was reborn in a place of joy.”
dhpak1.14:9.3: Then the Teacher said to him: “It is even so, householder. They that are heedful, be they lay folk or monastics,
dhpak1.14:9.4: rejoice both in this world and in the world beyond.” So saying, he pronounced the following verse:
dhpak1.14:10.1: 18. Idha nandati, pecca nandati, katapuñño ubhayattha nandati, “Puññaṁ mĕ katan”-ti nandati, bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.
dhpak1.14:11.1: Here she’s happy, after death she’s happy, the righteous one’s happy in both places,
dhpak1.14:11.2: she’s happy, thinking: “I have done merit,” gone to a good fate, she’s happy much more.
dhpak1.14:12.1: At the end of the verse many became Stream-enterers and so on, and benefit arose to many people from the Dhamma teaching.
